title: The Killing form when the radical vanishes
statement:
Let $L$ be any field of characteristic zero, and let $\mathfrak l$ be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over $L$ [def-wf-lie-algebra]. Its radical $\operatorname{rad}\mathfrak l$ is the sum of all its solvable ideals [def-wf-lie-radical-centre]. If $\operatorname{rad}\mathfrak l=0$, the Killing form
$$B(x,y)=\operatorname{tr}_{\mathfrak l}(\operatorname{ad}x\circ\operatorname{ad}y)$$
is nondegenerate and $[\mathfrak l,\mathfrak l]=\mathfrak l$.

proof.text: Write $K=\{x:B(x,y)=0\ (y\in\mathfrak l)\}$. The identities of [lem-ag-killing-form-identities] show that $K$ is an ideal: $B([a,x],y)=-B(x,[a,y])=0$ for $x\in K$. Restriction to this ideal gives $B_K(x,y)=B(x,y)=0$ for all $x,y\in K$, in particular for $x\in[K,K]$.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: kernel ideal and equality of traces

proof.text: Choose an algebraic closure $E$ of $L$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and put $H=E\otimes_L K$, with bracket $[a\otimes x,b\otimes y]=ab\otimes[x,y]$. A finite basis of $K$ gives a finite basis of $H$ over $E$, so the coefficient conventions of [det-d-linear] apply here. For $u=1\otimes x$, the identity $\operatorname{ad}_H(u)(a\otimes z)=a\otimes[x,z]$ identifies its adjoint with $1\otimes\operatorname{ad}_K(x)$; products agree by evaluation on pure tensors. The trace clause of [lem-ag-trace-solvability-scalar-extension] gives $B_H(1\otimes x,1\otimes y)=\iota(B_K(x,y))=0$. Bilinearity gives $B_H=0$, since pure tensors span $H$. Let $\rho:H\to\operatorname{End}_E(H)$ be the adjoint representation [def-wf-lie-algebra], and $A=\rho(H)$. Lift brackets and linear combinations to get $[A,A]=\rho([H,H])$. Thus $X\in[A,A]$, $Y\in A$ have lifts $u\in[H,H]$, $v\in H$, and $\operatorname{tr}_H(XY)=B_H(u,v)=0$. Apply [sk-lem-walg-trace-criterion] over the algebraically closed characteristic-zero field $E$: $A$ is solvable.

source.place: Proof, trace-criterion application to the adjoint image; scalar-extension repair E1(a), using Mathlib Trace.lean:378 and Solvable.lean:148,301

proof.text: Here $\ker\rho=Z(H)$, since $\rho(u)=0$ means $[u,H]=0$. Choose $n$ with $D^nA=0$. Starting at $\rho(H)=A$, preservation of brackets and linearity inductively give $\rho(D^rH)\subseteq D^rA$ [def-wf-lie-algebra]. Thus $D^nH\subseteq Z(H)$ and $D^{n+1}H=0$, so $H$ is solvable. Descend by [lem-ag-trace-solvability-scalar-extension] to get $K$ solvable over $L$. As a solvable ideal, $K\subseteq\operatorname{rad}\mathfrak l=0$ [def-wf-lie-radical-centre]. Thus $K=0$ and $B$ is nondegenerate.

source.place: Proof, abelian kernel and vanishing of K; solvability descends from the scalar extension by Mathlib Solvable.lean:301

proof.text: Put $D=[\mathfrak l,\mathfrak l]$ and $D^\perp=\{z:B(d,z)=0\ (d\in D)\}$. If $z\in D^\perp$, invariance [lem-ag-killing-form-identities] gives $B(x,[y,z])=B([x,y],z)=0$ for every $x,y$. Symmetry and nondegeneracy give $[y,z]=0$ for every $y$, so $z\in Z(\mathfrak l)$. Conversely, for central $z$ the same identity gives $B([x,y],z)=0$, hence vanishing on their linear span. Thus $D^\perp=Z(\mathfrak l)$.

source.place: Proof, displayed equality of the orthogonal complement and the centre

proof.text: The centre is an ideal by the Jacobi identity and its brackets vanish, so its first derived term is zero [def-wf-lie-algebra]. It is therefore solvable and lies in the zero radical [def-wf-lie-radical-centre]. Hence $D^\perp=0$. Apply [lem-ag-bilinear-double-orthogonal] to the symmetric, now nondegenerate $B$ on finite-dimensional $\mathfrak l$: $D=(D^\perp)^\perp=0^\perp=\mathfrak l$, since $B(0,x)=0$ for every $x$.

source.place: Proof, last sentence: centre vanishes and the derived algebra is the whole algebra
